reviewFindings: Authorization/side-effects: the slash-command admission is evaluated BEFORE any side effect. Verified with a probe that a denied '/bind s1' leaves store.get('bind:telegram:42') === undefined (no binding written) and '/quiet s1' denied does not write router state. The known-slash branch calls control.admit() and only then fireAsync(routeAdmitted(...)); the denied branch replies and returns without touching handleCommand.

One admission path, not two: every action now funnels through the SAME control core. Session-affecting commands (stop/steer/ordinary-message) use the pre-existing canAcceptCommand via control.handle; the registry/conversation commands (help/status/bind/unbind/agent/route/tasks/sessions/use/quiet/unquiet/log) use the new control.admit -> admitCommand. Both read the same normalized policy and the same per-session overlay resolver, so a per-session policy applies identically. No parallel policy engine was created.

converse=false is not bypassable: an unknown slash is refused (t.unknownCommand) rather than echoed-then-delivered to the agent; a known slash that fails its minimum condition is refused with a reason; media-only text goes through the same ordinary-message gate; the legacy control===null path also refuses unknown slash and does not deliver. The only remaining route to the agent is a control-core 'accepted' verdict (or the control===null legacy ordinary-text path, which is never used by production wiring).

Adversarial probe found and FIXED a real bypass during this task: the task-selection numbered reply (a bare '1' resolving an ambiguity selection card) delivered the stored original message to the agent even under converse=false, because that resolution lived inside routeUnsafe before the gate. It is now admitted as a resource-access action (COMMAND_POLICY.bind = assets) but ONLY on the strength of a live pending row for the exact same (channel,accountId,userId,chatId) source — a wrong-source client sees no pending and falls through to the ordinary-message gate. Probes confirm: no assets -> rejected + pending kept; assets -> delivered once.

Adversarial finding: approval/question (button + numbered reply) do NOT require `converse` — they require `approve` (default true). This is correct per CONTRACTS §命令政策最小表 (approval/answer/action = live pending + correct source + validity + authorization + durable single claim), and it is not a converse bypass because settlement goes to the approval/question waiter, never to the agent conversation. The focused tests assert approve=false denies button + numbered reply + question reply (fail-closed) and that a wrong-source clicker cannot settle.

Group/source fail-closed: the QQ group path (channel lowercased === 'qq' && chatScope==='group') and the generic isGroupChat && caps.groupChatControl !== true path both return group_chat_disabled for every command shape. QQ unknown chatType returns source_chat_type_unknown. The group denial now runs inside admitCommand too, so registry commands (help/status/…) are covered by the same rule, not just the session commands. Group OUTBOUND notifications are unaffected (they never pass this ingress).

Two new opt-in capabilities (assets, quiet) were added to normalizeSessionPolicy (default off). This is a policy-shape extension (CONTRACTS: 新增字段同步types/projection/UI/测试). Without it, bind/use/quiet/unquiet would have been silently always-denied (the first implementation read caps.assets/caps.quiet off a capabilities object that never carried them) — caught by the reverse-review probe, fixed, and re-verified.

/log owner proof: the admission seam keeps the EXISTING owner determination (identity.list(channel) role === 'owner', channel-scoped, fail-closed when identity is missing/throws) via the ownerProof option rather than introducing a policy.owner requirement, so an identity owner is not locked out; policy.owner equality remains an alternative proof. An owner with the feature disabled still reaches t.logDisabled (feature switch), not a false 'not owner'.

Strings/diagnostics: invalid-token/invalid-chat errors return a generic '远程控制被拒绝' (t.controlRejected) — message content is never echoed back beyond the command token, and no source/account value is disclosed.
reviewResolution: Replaced the pre-existing `command === null -> routeUnsafe` fall-through with an explicit SLASH_COMMAND_ADMISSION map + control.admit gate; unknown slash now returns t.unknownCommand and returns without delivery.

Kept the control===null legacy path but made it (a) refuse unknown slash and (b) still resume a live task-selection (provenance recomputed from taskSelection.get(envelope)), so the existing task-selection integration tests and any non-control caller keep working without weakening the control-attached path.

Moved the task-selection resume OUT of routeUnsafe's body-affecting position and up behind its own assets admission (with short-circuit resume) so a resolved session can no longer route a selection reply through the ordinary-message converse gate or bypass it.

Made admissionDeniedText map each reason (group_chat_disabled / source_chat_type_unknown / owner_only / capability_required:converse / default) to a specific receipt so the user is never left in a black hole.
Extended normalizeSessionPolicy with assets/quiet and updated the one session-arbiter test that deep-equals the capability shape.

Updated the 4 existing tests that encoded the OLD (buggy) 'unknown slash is delivered as text' behavior: they now assert explicit refusal + zero agent delivery, and the /stop-with-appendage case still asserts no cancellation. This is encoded behavior change, not a test weakening: the security assertion (no delivery) is strictly stronger than before.
limitations: T04 is validated with the real bus + conversation router + Control Core via controlled envelopes (local-contract). It was NOT re-booted in a disposable DSH profile for this task (the T02 boot already established plugin activation; the admission gate is a pure JS contract that runs identically in-host). No host-only behavior is claimed for T04.

The approval/question button + numbered-reply paths are asserted through the real bridges with a stub interactive channel; no real IM card callback is exercised (no real accounts). The button path additionally relies on the pre-existing approval source checks (pushedTo/userId), which are unchanged by T04.

assets/quiet are new capabilities with no admin-UI toggle yet; they are set via inbound.control.capabilities in config. An owner enabling them from the Native/Recovery console would need the config surface (not added here; the overlay API intentionally cannot carry capabilities — normalizeControlOverlay drops them).

The `/agent` and `/unbind` aliases are admitted under the `bind` (assets) row, and `/route` under `status`; this groups aliases with their base command rather than giving each its own capability, which matches the minimum-table intent.

The steer classify/gate checks text.startsWith(steerPrefix) on the merged text; a text that begins with a custom steerPrefix is a steer regardless of a later '/', which is the pre-existing steer semantic and is now gated by converse.
